title: Watch List
markdown:
**What it is:** The things your Executive watches in the outside world for you: share prices, news and blog feeds, vendor status pages, SEC filings, web searches, and changes to specific web pages. You say what to watch and when to be told. That is the only filter.

**What it does:**

- Say what to watch in your own words and check the plan before it starts, or set it up by hand.
- Lists what is being watched, grouped by kind. Each card shows its name, **Tells you when** (what makes it speak), the last thing it told you (or *Has not told you anything yet*), what the last check found and why it stayed quiet, and the goal or person it is for. Click a group's heading to fold it.
- Tells you whenever a watch's own **Tells you when** is met. What it tells you shows up in your briefing, the same way an email or a Slack message does. Nothing else holds a change back: the same story twice is told once, and a busy page is summed up once a day.
- Pause or resume a watch without deleting it, or have it **Watch quietly**.
- Ties a watch to a goal and to a person on your team, so what it tells you goes to that person and the goal lists what is watching it.
- Review watches the Executive suggests before they go live.
- Asks whether to make a watch quieter when you keep dismissing what it tells you.
- Edit the whole list from chat as well as here.

**How to use:**

1. Open **Work** in the sidebar and pick the **Watch list** tab. At the top, type what you want watched in **What should I watch?**, e.g. *"Tell me if Initech's stock moves more than 8%"* or *"Let me know when Globex posts about pricing"*, and click **Set it up**. Names of your competitors, vendors and tickers from your company profile are understood.
2. **Here's what I'll watch** shows the plan in three plain lines: what it watches, when it tells you, and how often it checks. Nothing is saved yet.
   - **Start watching** adds it as shown.
   - **Change something** opens the form below with everything filled in, so you can adjust it and click **Start watching**.
   - If it can't be watched (too vague, or a link that isn't public), it says why. Add a detail and try again.
3. To skip the plain-words step, open **Set it up by hand**. Pick **What kind** and fill in **What to watch** (see the table below), with an optional **Name** and **Notes** (up to 500 characters). Under **More options**:
   - **Tells you when (optional)** narrows what makes it speak; leave it blank for the usual (see the table). The line under it says it in words, e.g. *As it stands: It moves 5% or more in a day, up or down.*
   - **How often it checks**, from *As often as it can* to *Once a week*. A watch never checks faster than its kind allows (see the note below).
4. Click **Start watching**. A news feed is checked first: it must load as a feed with posts. An address that loads as a readable page with no feed is added as a **Page change** watch instead; anything else is refused with the reason.
5. Use the switch on a card to pause or resume it. A paused watch does not check until you switch it back on.
6. Click the card (or **Open details** in its **⋯**) to open its page. Under its name it says how often it checks, e.g. *It checks every 15 minutes.* There you can:
   - switch **When something changes** between **Alert me** and **Watch quietly** (it keeps checking and keeps a record, and doesn't tell you);
   - read **What it does**:
     - **Tells you when**, with **Change**. For a share price, set the percent. For filings, tick the kinds. For the rest, list words it must mention, and tick **Only big changes** to hear less.
     - **Last told you**: when, and what, with **Open** for the source.
     - **Last checked**: when, what it found, and why it stayed quiet, e.g. *18 min ago: Down 1.1% today. Under 5%, so it stayed quiet.*
     - **It is for**: a goal, a person on your team, or both, with **Change**. With a person set, what it tells you goes to them. With a goal set, the goal on the **Goals** page lists it under *Watching*.
     - **Told you**: how many times it told you, and how many of those you dismissed.
     - **Added by**: you or the Executive.
   - edit **Notes** (saved when you click away);
   - read **What it told you**, the list of everything it has told you, newest first;
   - answer *"You dismissed 6 of the last 8 alerts from this. Only tell you about bigger changes?"* when most of what it told you lately was dismissed (at least 6 of the last 8). The first button makes it quieter: a share price needs twice the move (5% becomes 10%); any other watch tells you about big changes only. Either way **Tells you when** says so. **Stop watching** opens the delete confirmation. **Keep as is** leaves it alone. Whichever you pick, it doesn't ask again until a new run is dismissed too;
   - remove it with **Stop watching** in the **⋯** at the top, then confirm.
7. A watch the Executive added shows *added by the Executive* and has **Stop watching** choices in its **⋯**, each with a reason:
   - **Not relevant** removes it, and the Executive won't suggest that company or topic again;
   - **Too noisy** keeps it, and it tells you about big changes only;
   - **Wrong source** removes only this feed or page; the topic can still be watched another way.
8. Check **Suggested by the Executive** now and then. These are things the Executive thinks are worth watching but wants your OK on first. Each card shows what it is about, what would make it speak, the goal, person or department it is for, when it was suggested, and how many changes it has noticed so far. **Approve** turns it on. The **⋯** has **Decline** with the same three reasons as **Stop watching**; declining as *Too noisy* turns it on for big changes only. A suggestion never tells you anything until approved, and a declined one isn't suggested again.

| What kind | What to watch | Tells you when (example) |
|---|---|---|
| Stock | The ticker, e.g. `AAPL` | `{"abs_change_pct_gte": 5}` (usual: a 5% move in a day) |
| News | The address of a news or blog feed | `{"keywords": ["pricing", "launch"]}` |
| Vendor status | The address of the vendor's status page feed | `{"keywords": ["degraded", "outage"]}` |
| SEC filings | Ticker or CIK, e.g. `AAPL` or `320193` | `{"forms": ["8-K"]}` (usual: 8-K, 10-K, 10-Q) |
| Page change | The address of a public page | `{"keywords": ["price"]}` (usual: any change) |
| Web search (billed) | What to search for, e.g. `Acme Corp layoffs OR funding` | `{"keywords": ["acquisition"]}` |

Add `"only_big": true` to any of these except a stock to hear about big changes only.

**From chat:** *"Watch Apple stock and tell me about 5% moves."* · *"What are we watching right now?"* · *"Stop watching that competitor's blog, it's too noisy."* · *"Send what the Globex pricing watch finds to Sam."* Chat can change anything about a watch: what makes it speak, how often it checks, and the goal or person it is for.

*Note: each kind has a fastest pace: vendor status pages every 5 minutes, share prices every 15 minutes, news feeds every 30 minutes, SEC filings every hour, and page changes and web searches every 6 hours. A web search watch runs a paid AI web search on every check, so use them sparingly.*
